auth.description: Notion integration token sent as a bearer — an internal integration token or an OAuth-issued access token
auth.name: notion.token
auth.subject: unstated

config.help: Create an integration at notion.so/my-integrations and copy its Internal Integration Secret. **Then share your pages with it**: in Notion, open each page or database, use the ••• menu → Connections → and add your integration. An integration can only see content that has been shared with it this way, so a token that is otherwise valid returns a 404 for a page you can see in your browser until you do. Sharing a parent page shares everything under it
config.label: Integration token
config.name: token

description: Notion workspace: read a page's properties, query a database, search shared content, and create a page

operations.description: Get the bot user this integration authenticates as, confirming the token resolves and naming the workspace it belongs to. Takes no parameters

bot.description: The integration's owner and workspace name

operations.description: Get one page's properties, parent, icon, cover and timestamps. This does NOT return the page's text — in Notion a page's content is a separate tree of blocks, which this connector cannot read

params.description: The page's id, a UUID. It is the last path segment of the page's URL, where it appears without hyphens — either spelling is accepted
params.name: page_id

parent.description: Where the page lives: `{type: "database_id", database_id}`, `{type: "page_id", page_id}` or `{type: "workspace"}`

properties.description: The page's property values, keyed by property name. For a page in a database the keys are that database's own columns, so they are known only at runtime; for a page with a page parent there is exactly one, `title`

operations.description: Query a database and return its first page of entries (up to 100), unfiltered and in the database's default order. Each entry is a page, and its `properties` are keyed by that database's own column names. Direction remains conservatively authored as write pending individual review; POST is transport only and supplied no evidence

params.description: The database's id, a UUID. Open the database as a full page in Notion and it is the last path segment of the URL — not the id of a page inside it
params.name: database_id

has_more.description: True when the database holds more entries than this page returned. This connector cannot fetch them — the cursor is an opaque token and no query parameter is encodable (C-30)

next_cursor.description: The cursor for the next page. Unusable here, for the reason given on `has_more`

results.description: The matching pages, each with its own `properties` object keyed by the database's column names

operations.description: Search the pages and databases shared with this integration by title, returning the first page of matches (up to 100). Notion matches on title only — it does not search page text. Direction remains conservatively authored as write pending individual review; POST is transport only and supplied no evidence

params.description: The text to match against page and database titles. An empty string returns everything shared with the integration
params.name: query

has_more.description: True when more matches exist than this page returned. This connector cannot fetch them — see notion-database-query

results.description: The matching pages and databases, newest first

operations.description: Create a new empty page as a child of an existing page. The page is created with a title and no content — this connector cannot write page body text, which in Notion is a separate tree of blocks. The parent page must be shared with this integration

params.description: The id of the existing page to create this page inside, a UUID. It must be a page, not a database, and it must be shared with this integration
params.name: parent_page_id

params.description: The page title as Notion rich text: a list of runs, each `{"text": {"content": "..."}}`. A plain title is one run — `[{"text": {"content": "My page"}}]`
params.name: title

content.description: The literal text of this run

link.description: An optional link on this run, `{"url": "..."}`

id.description: The created page's id, which is what later calls address it by
